# Integrated Wald Inference Workbench

Repository: https://github.com/reblocke/conf_curve_likelihood
Deployed app: https://reblocke.github.io/conf_curve_likelihood/
Purpose: Backward-compatible integrated browser workbench for documented one-parameter Wald
reconstruction, compatibility, normalized relative support, and repeated-study design calibration
Status: No manuscript version is expected. Code and teaching examples are repository-authored unless otherwise noted.
App version: 0.2.4
Numerical core: wald-inference 0.4.1
Core release: https://github.com/reblocke/wald-inference-core/releases/tag/v0.4.1
Core wheel SHA-256: d7272023f65088729d3ff997cab7cac57b84f22ac6108244ec2170434557d99b

## Human-Readable Entry Points
- `README.md` is the primary human-facing overview.
- Core numerical scope:
  https://github.com/reblocke/wald-inference-core/blob/v0.4.1/docs/SCIENTIFIC_SCOPE.md
- `docs/SCIENTIFIC_SCOPE.md` defines this integrated workbench's two conditioning paradigms,
  assumptions, outputs, and non-goals.
- `docs/VALIDATION.md` defines frozen parity, formula ownership, browser/privacy/accessibility,
  release, and evidence gates.
- Focused-tool chooser:
  https://reblocke.github.io/wald-inference-tools/
- `docs/adr/0002-released-core-and-generated-browser-stage.md` records dependency ownership,
  staging, upgrade, and rollback.
- `docs/MAINTENANCE.md` and `docs/PRIVACY.md` record the feature-freeze and browser data boundary.
- `docs/migration/` preserves the frozen pre-split API, browser contract, and validation authority.
- `CHANGELOG.md` records app release notes and exact core provenance.

## Repository Layout
- `src/confcurve/`: legacy compatibility API, browser payload models, app orchestration, staging
- `web/`: static GitHub Pages app
- `web/assets/py/`: ignored generated `wald_inference` + `confcurve` browser bundle and manifest
- `scripts/stage_web_python.py`: deterministic staging entrypoint called by `make stage-web`
- `tests/golden/`: frozen 22-case B01-B08 behavior corpus
- `tests/e2e/`: semantic Chromium/WebKit browser checks
- `docs/`: decisions, migration records, workflow notes, and scientific interpretation guardrails

## Data and Reuse Boundaries
No clinical data expected

## Workflow
```text
uv sync --locked
make stage-web
make verify
make serve
```

`make serve`, local tests, CI, Pages, and releases all use `make stage-web`. Generated Python is
never hand-edited or committed. A clean clone resolves the exact core release through `uv.lock`; it
does not require a sibling repository.

## Dependencies
`pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` are authoritative. Numerical formulas belong to released
`wald-inference`; `confcurve` must contain only compatibility and app-specific orchestration.
`web/assets/py/manifest.json` records app/core versions, source commit, file sizes and SHA-256
digests, and an aggregate bundle digest. Browser startup verifies the complete manifest before
imports.

## Citation
No publication DOI is assigned to this repository. Cite the GitHub repository URL and the commit or release used.

## Agent Cautions
- Never implement, copy, or modify a core-owned formula in `confcurve`; release it upstream first.
- Preserve the frozen `confcurve.__all__`, `compute_curves()` schema/order/types, warnings,
  strict-JSON behavior, UI defaults, exports, and explanatory copy.
- Pin only exact released core artifacts with reviewed checksums.
- Do not re-add a README appendix aimed primarily at LLMs; integrate user-facing details into normal README sections.
- Keep restricted clinical data, private drafts, publisher PDFs, local paths, and generated outputs out of public documentation unless explicitly reviewed.
- Prefer concise summaries plus links to citable records over copied manuscript or publisher text.
